A1.justification: Both PDFs describe T-JEPA and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The complete documents support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original T-JEPA classification/regression experiments, representation analyses, regularization-token ablations, and an I-JEPA retraining experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds MNIST evaluations and additional experiments with competing self-supervised methods.

M1.justification: The encoders, EMA update, predictor, and loss remain unchanged in Section 3. New Appendix H specifies dropping [REG] from encoded targets and predictor inputs, but Section 3 in both versions says it is never masked. This unresolved discrepancy prevents confidently distinguishing additional implementation explanation from a procedural revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST as a 784-feature, ten-class tabular classification benchmark. The six original tabular datasets and the ImageNet-1K collapse comparison remain, making this a limited extension of coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds SubTab and explicit ResNet comparisons for BinRecon and VIME. Conversely, PTaRL comparisons with DCNv2, AutoInt, and FT-Transformer in v1 Table 6 disappear. This substantially revises comparator participation beyond merely extending existing methods to MNIST.

E3.justification: The SSL evaluation is reorganized around MLP/ResNet downstream configurations, including new ResNet experiments, and introduces average-rank aggregation instead of win summaries. Appendix F reports replacing several literature-derived evaluations with original experiments. The 80/10/10 splits and accuracy/RMSE metrics remain; baseline tuning is inconsistently described as Bayesian optimization in Appendix F and default settings in F.1.

E4.justification: The epoch-wise intra- and inter-feature variance analysis is removed from v1 Table 2 and Section 5.1. The regularization-token ablation, collapse comparison, alternative masking/predictor investigations, and separate feature-importance analysis remain. New Figure 7 explains the pipeline rather than adding an ablation.

E5.justification: v1 reports uncertainty principally for T-JEPA, with imported baseline means averaged over ten runs. v2 Tables 1–2 report twenty-run summaries and standard deviations across substantially more baselines and SSL methods, explicitly marking SwitchTab uncertainty unavailable. Appendix F distinguishes newly supplied PTaRL deviations from newly performed experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds MNIST and SubTab results, separate SSL/downstream-model results, and average ranks, while removing some PTaRL and variance entries. Comparator summaries also change: XGBoost CA RMSE changes from 0.462 to 0.433, and MLP+PTaRL ALOI accuracy from 0.964 to 0.917. These involve revised experimental provenance, not established same-setting gains. T-JEPA means on the six retained datasets are unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Equation (8), defining averaged intra- and inter-feature variances, is removed. The core method equations and alternative-strategy mathematics remain, while the KL-divergence and uniformity definitions move to Appendix G. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: augmentation-free tabular JEPA, downstream performance improvements and GBDT competitiveness, identification of relevant features without labels, and regularization tokens for escaping collapse.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly interprets increasing KL divergence and distance as improved alignment, and uniformity as information preservation. Section 5.3 qualifies feature-level interpretation because attention mixes tokens. The variance-specialization explanation and v1's comments about PTaRL's limited-data advantages and computational complexity are removed; the concluding limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendices B and F provide downstream architecture descriptions, dataset-specific and default hyperparameters, comparator settings, and detailed result provenance. Appendix H documents [REG] routing and the use of one token outside the ablation. MNIST compute information is added. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the existing code URL is merely relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds the PaCMAP reference and explicitly identifies SubTab as the closest related approach, distinguishing reconstruction space and contrastive training. Appendix F.2 expands descriptions of already cited SSL methods. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Sections 4.2 and 5.1 are substantially reorganized around downstream/SSL comparisons and alignment/uniformity. SSL performance material moves into the main text, metric definitions move to Appendix G, and the appendices gain separate architecture, comparator-setting, and regularization-token explanations. This substantially changes the exposition despite retaining the introduction, core method, and conclusion.

P2.justification: The main performance displays are redesigned with MNIST, uncertainty, and average-rank columns; the representation table loses its variance rows. Numerous hyperparameter tables and Figure 7 are added, Figure 1 is revised, and Figure 3's caption is expanded. The underlying images in Figures 2–6 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through detailed hyperparameters, broader uncertainty reporting, and evaluation of the closely related SubTab method, addressing gaps in v1's literature-derived comparisons. The benefit is limited by removing PTaRL comparisons for three downstream architectures and by unresolved baseline-tuning and [REG]-handling inconsistencies. The evidence supports a modest overall improvement, without establishing stronger general superiority.
